title: The Glasshouse Alarm
overview: An overnight alarm and a burst irrigation pipe damage a rare-plant greenhouse. The first explanation is equipment failure, but the timing appears unusual.
objective: Determine whether the damage was accidental or deliberately arranged, and identify the strongest corroborated explanation.

hypotheses.statement: A contractor deliberately opened the drain valve to conceal an unauthorized attempt to remove plants.
A pressure fault caused a pipe failure and accidental flooding.

evidence.title: Facilities incident report
evidence.content: Water was found across the propagation room at 2:16 AM. Several rare seedlings were missing from a locked cabinet.

evidence.title: Greenhouse access roster
evidence.content: Horticulturist Jules Moreno, contractor Cal Rusk, and night custodian Mei Lin held authorized access during the week.

evidence.title: Irrigation control log
evidence.content: The drain valve was manually opened at 1:48 AM using the maintenance override. Pressure sensors remained within normal range before the valve opened.

evidence.title: Contractor work order
evidence.content: Cal Rusk's temporary override code was used outside the scheduled work window. His work order was closed the previous afternoon.

evidence.title: Custodian's observation
evidence.content: Mei Lin saw a covered plant cart leave through the loading bay shortly before the alarm, although no plant transfer was scheduled.

suspects.name: Cal Rusk
suspects.role: Contractor whose override code opened the valve

witness_statements.statement: She saw a covered plant cart leave the loading bay shortly before the alarm.

timeline.event: Cal Rusk's work order was closed.
The irrigation drain valve was manually opened while pressure remained normal.
A covered plant cart left the loading bay.
Water damage and missing seedlings were reported.
